title: ANAKINRA IN THE TREATMENT OF PEDIATRIC ACUTE MYOCARDITIS
official: ANAKINRA IN THE TREATMENT OF PEDIATRIC ACUTE MYOCARDITIS. ANAPEM
summary: Main objective: To compare the efficacy of Anakinra vs placebo, on top of the standard of care, on restoration of myocardial function at 3 days following treatment initiation, in children admitted for acute myocarditis in intensive care units.

interventions.name: Kineret 100 mg/0.67 ml solution for injection in pre-filled syringe.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Children from ≥ 3 months to < 18 years of age
2. Hospitalized in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) for acute myocarditis defined as : - a reduced left ventricle ejection fraction below 50%  and  - troponin T rise (>1.5x normal range)
3. Signed informed consent by legal representative and patient according to the legislation.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Children weighing less than 5 Kgs
2. Anti TNF-α within the past 14 days
3. Malignancy or history of malignancy or any comorbidity limiting survival or conditions predicting inability to complete the study
4. Ongoing or recent use of any other medication Known inhibitors/inducers of cytochrome P450
5. -	Patients with increased risk of Tuberculosis (TB ) infection -	Recent tuberculosis infection or with active TB o	Close contact with a patient with TB o	Patients recently arrived less than 3 months from a country with high prevalence of TB o	A chest radiograph suggestive of TB
6. -	Patients with overt concomitant bacterial infection
7. -	Patients with overt concomitant bacterial infection
8. -	Patients with any type of immunodeficiency or cancer
9. - Inability of the legal representative (and the patient, when applicable) to understand the national language (French)
10. Pregnancy** or breastfeeding
11. No affiliation to the Social Security
12. Current enrollment in another clinical trial
13. Known anterior cardiomyopathy or operated cardiopathy
14. Neutropenia  (< 1,5 × 10^9 /L).
15. Known hypersensitivity to Anakinra or any of its excipients (citric acid anhydrous, sodium chloride, disodium EDTA dihydrate, polysorbate 80, E. coli derived proteins)
16. Administration of a live vaccine in the 4 weeks prior to inclusion
17. Hepatitis B infection, defined as positive HBsAg and/or detectable HBV DNA (PCR).   Due to the urgent need to start treatment, inclusion may occur before hepatitis B screening results are available. If hepatitis B infection is subsequently confirmed, the study treatment will be immediately discontinued.
